Code an agent wants to run is a high-risk action that a person must approve. There is an optional mode, off by default, in which code that only touches the agent's own files runs without approval; turning it on requires org:manage and an explicit risk acknowledgement, and it is audited. Code runs in a container with no network, a read-only file system, no capabilities, no privilege escalation, an unprivileged user and limits on processes, memory and CPU. gVisor is optional. The executor service mounts the host's Docker socket, which is equivalent to administrator access to the host. We recommend running it only on a dedicated, trusted host. It is not part of the public deployment.

Public traffic arrives over HTTPS: the Caddy proxy terminates TLS with automatic certificates and sends a one-year Strict-Transport-Security header on the site and the application. On the application it adds X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and Referrer-Policy. Files uploaded by users and artifacts are served with a sandbox CSP so they cannot run code on the application's origin. Between containers, inside a private network on the same server, the connection to Postgres does not use TLS (sslmode=disable). Secrets are encrypted at the application level, but we have not verified encryption at rest of the hosting provider's disks. There is no global Content-Security-Policy

A cron job takes a compressed Postgres dump every night (03:30, server time). It is stored on the same server with restrictive permissions and kept for 14 days; the script fails with a message if the file is suspiciously small. There is no off-server copy and no formal recovery time or recovery point objective. Continuous integration builds and tests the backend and the runtime, builds the frontend and runs the race detector on key packages, end-to-end tests, a Dockerfile linter, govulncheck and npm audit (the last two do not block). Images are published tagged by commit.

If you found a security issue in AI Workforce OS, we want to know. We are a small team: there is no bug bounty and no guaranteed timelines, but every report is read, investigated and answered.

E-mail info@workforceai.es with the subject "Vulnerability". It is the same contact our security.txt (RFC 9116) publishes. Describe the problem, the affected component, the steps to reproduce it and the impact you believe it has. A minimal proof of concept helps a lot. Do not include real third-party data. If you accidentally accessed data that is not yours, do not keep it and tell us in the report. We do not publish a PGP key today. If you need to send something sensitive, write to us first and we will agree on an encrypted channel. You can write in Spanish or English.

We are especially interested in: data leaks between organizations, bypass of authentication, SSO, MFA or permissions, bypass of approvals, spending caps or the kill switch, exposure of credentials or secrets, abuse of signed approval links, SSRF through webhooks or web tools, and tampering with the audit chain. The public site workforceai.es. The application at app.workforceai.es, its API (/api/v1), the token-based public API (/api/public/v1) and the WebSocket (/ws). The product's code: Go backend, Python agent runtime and frontend.

Third-party services: AI model providers, hosting, e-mail and the services each customer connects. Denial of service, load testing and massive or noisy automated scanning. Social engineering, phishing or physical access. Spam and reports that only point out a missing header or best practice without demonstrable impact. A trial account is a good place to research without touching anyone's data. Do not use it to degrade the service.

If you act in good faith and follow this policy, we will not take legal action against you or report you to the authorities for your research. Good faith means: Testing only what is needed to demonstrate the issue. Not accessing, modifying or deleting other people's data beyond the bare minimum. Not degrading the service and not extorting. Not publishing details until it is fixed, giving us a reasonable time to do so. This text is a statement of intent, not a contract, and it cannot bind third parties such as our providers. It is pending review by a lawyer.
